title: Spell checklists live outside the Atlas in GitHub, bound to it only by a registry and a duty to check for freshness
content:
The Atlas does not contain the checklists that govern Spell work. A.1.10.2.5.1.3 requires only that "all Spell Checklists must be recorded in the Spell Checklists Registry," with each entry carrying "Name," "Type (Core Spell Checklist, Agent Spell Checklist, or Operational Checklist)" and "URL." The registry itself is Active Data whose "Responsible Party is the Core Spell Teams" and whose "Update Process must follow the protocol for 'Direct Edit'" (A.1.10.2.5.1.3.2).

This is a deliberate boundary. Checklist content changes frequently and is maintained by engineers in a repository with pull requests and review; routing every step edit through Atlas governance would either paralyze the checklists or trivialize the Atlas. Instead the Atlas governs *which* documents are authoritative and *who* may change them, and delegates the content.

The cost is that the operative rules live in mutable external files. The Atlas addresses this from two directions: the two-approvals-one-per-team requirement constrains who can change the content, and A.1.10.2.5.2 imposes a duty on the reader — "Users must verify their local copy is aligned with the latest version in the Ecosystem Operational References repository **before each use** of the reference materials."

That freshness duty is the interesting piece. With a cached copy of a living document, following the checklist faithfully is not enough; you can be diligently compliant with a superseded version. Making re-verification a per-use obligation treats staleness as a failure mode in its own right.

The registry is what keeps the arrangement honest. Without it, "the checklist" would be whatever file someone remembered, and there would be no way to enumerate the rules in force.
description: A.1.10.2.5.1.3 records name, type and URL as Active Data maintained by Direct Edit, and A.1.10.2.5.2 requires users to verify their local copy before each use.
